data.body: Phase 1 confirmed RCA (runtime proof, no source edits): tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_wiki_render_corpus.py:318-327 implements two existential claims (`eligible > 0`, `changed > 0`) but exhausts all eligible prose units before asserting. A runtime trace through the real `_render_unit`/Pandoc path observed 232 calls, 199 changed witnesses, and 8.865s. The same control flow with an exact stop immediately after both witnesses were present observed 1 call and 0.036s. This rules out corpus loading and assertion overhead as the material cause: 231 unnecessary real Pandoc subprocess conversions account for 8.829s in the paired probe. Negative controls remained discriminating: an identity renderer made 232 calls but produced zero changed witnesses and failed the contract; an empty/no-eligible source made zero calls and failed the contract. The mechanism is therefore the missing exact existential short-circuit in this test loop. Defect legitimacy: this violates the ticket acceptance contract and the user requirement that individual tests be negligible while preserving coverage. Caller-dependency gate: the planned edit is confined to this one test; full-corpus safety, richness, and fixed-point consumers use `corpus_pass1` independently, so no caller behavior depends on exhaustive evaluation here. Expected post-fix behavior is identical pass/fail semantics with evaluation stopping only after both existential witnesses exist.
